label: One being whose esse is its essence is first cause of all others, from De ente
description: Composition of De ente c.3 [69874]'s three stages on one profile and one witness: at most one actual being is its own esse (b); hence every actual being other than it has represented esse unequal to its represented essence (a real distinction only if equality of represented principles is read as real identity; derived from b as in the passage's order, not from the intellectus-essentiae argument); every distinct esse goes back to a being whose esse is its essence (c); so one and the same such n heads a finite chain of actual causes of being to every other actual being, and, by no infinite regress, has no actual cause of its own esse. TwoSourcesControl shows at-most-one is needed. Mode of causing unspecified; no direct causation of every esse, conservation, efficiency, necessity, concreteness at a world or God identification follows.
